A B+-tree in a warehouse

parcel
a value; the plate on it shows its key
section
a leaf: up to 2k* = 16 parcels, sorted by key; it keeps its place on the rails
chain
the leaf chain: a chain links each section to its neighbour in key order, the pointers next and previous
free place
room to grow: the new section of a leaf split goes into the free place right next to the full section
room
an inner node: up to 2k = 8 keys on its front, 2k + 1 = 9 holes in its floor
chute
a pointer to a subtree; the sign over its hole gives the subtree's interval [a;b[
amber
new or moving
red
full, and a key must go in: the node splits first; with the new key, both halves hold at least k
green
found

Lecture 06a, B-trees (definition, queries, splits). The tree is the one the code's BPlusTree(8, 16) in system/indexes/btree.py builds for these keys; the notebook B-tree.ipynb builds and splits a smaller one. The keys are invented.
